A comment or a clarification answer cannot supply it, so the only way this fix-up can land on `ai/issue-7072` is for the body to carry that line. The branch name is already known from GitHub facts (`ai/issue-7072` exists at 8db02fe56238, the head of open PR #7076). The unblock judge already chose `operator_step`, so the person this needs has already been asked. Option B depends on PR #7076's review/autofix loop picking up a CI failure, which is not reliable, and it drops the tracked fix-up. Option C contradicts the issue ("do not add the exception on main") and would fail the audit on `main`.
Q2: The issue requires the audit test and CI on `ai/issue-7072` to pass. Gating the allowlist entry behind an unset env var would keep CI red (B). Making no test change at all (C) would not deliver the fix. `ISSUE_7248_TARGET_BRANCH_UNSET_OPERATOR_STEP` therefore stays an unread operator-step marker: the code it guards is the branch retargeting, which a person finishes by editing the body. No existing path on `main` changes. The entry goes into `ALLOWLIST_EXCEPTIONS` in `tests/test_workflow_checkout_integration_ref_audit.py` (line 22), and the classification assertion at lines 76 and 84 stays unchanged.

SETUP REQUIRED:
- ISSUE_7248_TARGET_BRANCH_UNSET_OPERATOR_STEP (variable, operator-step marker only; nothing reads it): an operator adds the line ``Target branch: `ai/issue-7072` `` to this issue's body and posts `/reclarify`. Until then, planning and implementation for this fix-up do not start, and `main` and every existing workflow, merge and release run unchanged.
